title: Introduce intermittent surge concession orchestrator and commitment rollback paths
author: Aisha Gupta
description: Motivation: In high multiplexing scenarios a small fraction of tenants cause repeated intermittent bursts that force aggressive preemption or large-scale overprovisioning. Rather than enlarging reserved fleets or increasing global headroom we introduce an "intermittent surge concession" pattern: allow a tenant to temporarily concede part of its committed throughput in exchange for prioritized fast-path recovery and a bounded rollback mechanism. This PR implements the orchestration, telemetry and safety checks for concessions and the commitment rollback path if capacity remains constrained. Design summary: 1) Concession orchestrator: a new controller evaluates short-window utilization signals and offers a concession token to eligible tenants; tokens specify duration, allowed throughput reduction and a recovery grace budget. 2) Proportional throttle adapter: when cluster pressure is detected, the router consults active concessions and applies proportional throttles rather than blunt preemption—this reduces latency regressions for other tenants. 3) Commitment rollback: if the orchestrator granted a concession but capacity did not free up within a configured patience window, the rollback manager transparently restores the tenant's reserved throughput (at the cost of evicting opportunistic warmlets) and emits an explainable audit event so customers can reconcile billing and QoS. 4) Safety and SLOs: we limit concession frequency per-tenant, track a decay-weighted concession score, and never allow concessions to reduce guaranteed latency SLOs below the emergency floor. 5) Telemetry: new metrics (concession_offers_total, concession_accept_rate, concession_rollback_total, concession_decay_score, concession_durations_seconds) and dashboard p99 impact views are included. Rollout plan: staged rollout in three phases: (A) controller + metrics (canary, read-only routing) on dedicated fleets; (B) enable proportional throttle with a 10% sample of tenants; (C) global enablement with opt-out per-tenant and a 7-day monitoring burn-in before updating billing signals. Migration notes: default behavior is opt-in per-tenant; no automatic changes to reserved capacity. Linear references: ENG-7321 (concession orchestration prototype), ENG-7489 (rollback safety harness). Why unique vs existing approaches: this is not a queue-based debt system; concessions are voluntary, timeboxed, and paired with an explicit rollback path that prioritizes restoring commitments instead of silently degrading service or inflating headroom. Security / compliance: audit events for concession grant/rollback are routed to existing audit log pipeline and include opaque reason codes to avoid leaking internal thresholds.
commits: init: add concession orchestrator controller; api: concession CRD, token struct and validation; runtime: proportional throttle adapter and router integration; autoscaler: rollback manager and eviction hooks; telemetry: metrics registry and dashboard config; tests: unit + e2e concession flow; docs: operational runbook and CLI flags

release_notes: Add 'Intermittent Surge Concessions' feature for Dedicated fleets: allows tenants to voluntarily reduce reserved throughput temporarily to avoid cluster-wide preemption; includes proportional throttling and automatic rollback. Opt-in by default. New telemetry and dashboards added (concession_offers_total, concession_accept_rate, concession_rollback_total).
